channel.title: Shah Spectrum
channel.description:
There's more to a headline than the headline.
Shah Spectrum is a daily briefing on finance, macroeconomy and technology. Each episode takes one story from the news and explains what happened, why it happened and why it matters, in about five minutes. No jargon, no hype, and no advice on what to buy or sell.
Narrated by an AI-generated voice. Made to explain the news, not as investment advice.
channel.itunes:subtitle: Finance, macroeconomy and tech, one layer deeper.

item.title: Hormuz and oil: what it means for India
item.description: The Strait of Hormuz has been disrupted since 28 February, and oil is still above 100 dollars a barrel. We explain why the strait matters, what Iran and the US each want before it fully reopens, and what it means for India's import bill. Sources: US Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy (16 Jun 2025); Reuters via BusinessDay (27 Oct 2026); DiscoveryAlert (28 Oct 2026); Down To Earth (26 Aug 2026); Free Press Journal (27 Aug 2026). Iran's conditions come from Iranian media and the US response is unpublished; prices change daily. Explanation only, not investment advice. Narrated by an AI-generated version of Mittal Shah's voice.

item.title: Southeast Asia's haze: what it costs
item.description: Smoke from Indonesia's fires has again reached Malaysia, Singapore and beyond. We explain what is burning, how smoke turns into a cost for schools, workplaces and hospitals, and why the question of who pays is still mostly unanswered. Sources: Copernicus/EU Space image of the day (20 Oct 2026); Down To Earth (21 Oct 2026); Eco-Business (16 Oct 2026). Cost figures are early estimates and burned-area figures are from one unconfirmed satellite analysis. Explanation only, not investment advice. Narrated by an AI-generated version of Mittal Shah's voice.

item.title: Big AI spending: when does it pay back?
item.description: Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta are spending hundreds of billions of dollars on computers for artificial intelligence. We explain why, what the cloud growth numbers show, and what would count as the money paying back. Sources: Meta Q2 2026 results release, SEC filing (Exhibit 99.1); Alphabet and Amazon Q2 2026 earnings call transcripts (Amazon call 7 Aug 2026); UpperEdge cloud growth summary (13 Aug 2026); Schwab market commentary (23 Oct 2026). Figures are company statements and plans, which can change. Explanation only, not investment advice. Narrated by an AI-generated version of Mittal Shah's voice.

item.title: Tesla and SpaceX are studying a merger
item.description: Tesla and SpaceX have each set up a committee of independent directors to look at a possible merger. We explain what was said on SpaceX's earnings call, why Elon Musk says AI is the reason, and why control and a high shareholder vote make this far from simple. No deal, price or timetable has been announced. Sources: Axios (20 Oct 2026), Gizmodo, CBS News, Euronews (22 Oct 2026), Electrek (19 Oct 2026); company filings not opened. Explanation only, not investment advice. Narrated by an AI-generated version of Mittal Shah's voice.

item.title: Foreign investors and Indian shares
item.description: Foreign investors have sold about 3.1 lakh crore rupees of Indian shares in 2026 so far, nearly double last year. We explain who they are, why they are selling, and what it means for India. Sources: Swarajya (18 Oct 2026), Angel One (12 Oct 2026), AIR News (11 Oct 2026), Tribune India (21 Jul 2026). Figures as reported from depository data. Explanation only, not investment advice. Narrated by an AI-generated version of Mittal Shah's voice.

item.title: France in turmoil: from school protests to a budget test
item.description: A weekend of riots in France began as school protests and has become a test of whether the government can fix its budget. We explain what happened, why the deficit and debt matter, and what could follow. Sources: Reuters explainer (19 Oct 2026, read via ThePrint), Euronews (2 and 18 Oct 2026), Korea Times (21 Oct 2026), The Week/AFP (18 Oct 2026). Explanation only, not investment advice. Narrated by an AI-generated version of Mittal Shah's voice.

item.title: India's emergency fund: why forex reserves fell
item.description: India's foreign exchange reserves fell by more than eight billion dollars in a single week, to about 726 billion dollars. We explain what the reserves are, why they move, and what the fall means for India. Explanation only, not investment advice. Narrated by an AI-generated version of Mittal Shah's voice.

item.title: Tesla's flying Roadster: spectacle or strategy?
item.description: Tesla unveiled a new Roadster that jumps, flips and lands using SpaceX-built thrusters. We explain how the technology works, why it is a showpiece rather than the real business, and what it signals for the car industry and for India. Explanation only, not investment advice. Narrated by an AI-generated version of Mittal Shah's voice.

item.title: Why the RBI raised interest rates while growth is strong
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India raised its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% and said rate cuts are off the table for now. We explain why it moved, what changed in its stance, and what it means for borrowers. Explanation only, not investment advice. Narrated by an AI-generated voice.
